cases.computed_description: snapshot data_kind = SYNTHETIC; 13 objects, all tagged
cases.expected_description: no fixture claims a real catalogue
cases.name: c0.fixtures_are_declared_synthetic
cases.notes: this milestone had no network access, so no Gaia DR3 record was retrieved. Writing plausible numbers under a real catalogue's name would be fabricating records and the gate would be verifying a fiction. tools/import_gaia.py is what produces fixtures with genuine provenance, as a separate optional step
cases.reference: every committed fixture is tagged SYNTHETIC or LITERATURE_FROM_MEMORY, and none claims to be retrieved catalogue data

cases.name: c0.unit_conversions_round_trip
cases.notes: the transverse-velocity factor is the one astrometry gets wrong most often, so it is checked against its definition rather than a quoted value
cases.reference: every boundary conversion round-trips, and 1 arcsec/yr at 1 pc is 4.740470446 km/s

cases.name: c0.speed_of_light_in_internal_units
cases.parameters: derived from c and the Julian year
cases.reference: 1 pc corresponds to 3.261563777 light-years, so c = 0.3066 pc/yr

cases.name: c0.ra_dec_to_unit_vector
cases.reference: the ICRS unit vector is correct at the cardinal directions, and the tangent basis (p_hat, q_hat) is orthonormal and orthogonal to r_hat

cases.expected_description: estimator InverseParallaxHighQuality, distance 10 pc
cases.name: c0.parallax_distance_high_quality
cases.reference: a parallax of 100 mas with signal-to-noise 200 yields exactly 10 pc by inverse parallax, with the estimator recorded

cases.computed_description: snr=2 flagged low-signal-to-noise; negative parallax flagged non-positive; both still in the catalogue
cases.expected_description: both rejected for inverse parallax, both retained
cases.name: c0.poor_parallax_is_rejected_not_inverted
cases.notes: d = 1/parallax is NOT a universally unbiased estimator, and the quality gate that licenses it lives in exactly one place. A source that fails it keeps its astrometry and loses only its distance
cases.reference: a source with parallax signal-to-noise 2 and one with a NEGATIVE parallax both get estimator None, with distinct reasons, and are RETAINED with a flag rather than deleted

cases.name: c0.proper_motion_convention_mu_alpha_star
cases.notes: the single test that distinguishes the two proper-motion conventions. mu_alpha* multiplies p_hat directly and is never divided by cos(dec) in the Cartesian conversion; the division appears only on the way back to a spherical coordinate
cases.parameters: dec = 60 deg, mu_alpha* = 500 mas/yr, 100 yr; measured d(ra)/dt / mu_alpha* = 2.0000e+00 (expected 2)
cases.reference: the catalogued pm_ra is mu_alpha* = mu_alpha cos(dec): at dec = 60 the coordinate rate d(ra)/dt comes out at mu_alpha*/cos(dec), twice the physical rate

cases.expected_description: transverse displacement fraction below 1e-12
cases.name: c0.radial_velocity_contribution_is_purely_radial
cases.notes: radial velocity positive means receding, so the radial displacement must be positive: the sign is asserted, not just the magnitude
cases.reference: a star with zero proper motion and positive radial velocity moves only along the line of sight

cases.name: c0.astrometry_cartesian_round_trip
cases.parameters: 11 sources, unit vector compared near the pole where right ascension is degenerate
cases.reference: observables -> barycentric Cartesian -> observables is the identity, for every fixture with a defensible distance

cases.name: c0.stationary_star_does_not_move
cases.notes: EXACT zero, not a tolerance: the propagation is x + v dt and v is identically zero, so any displacement at all would be a bug in the conversion
cases.reference: a source with zero proper motion and zero radial velocity has exactly zero displacement after 10 000 yr

cases.computed_description: 1000 yr displacement 9.6963e-02 pc; warning at 1e6 yr = yes, at 1e4 yr = no
cases.expected_description: measurable displacement; warning fires only outside the stated validity
cases.name: c0.high_proper_motion_propagation
cases.notes: rectilinear barycentric motion is a LOCAL KINEMATIC MODEL, not a Galactic orbit integrator, and the warning is how that limit is communicated rather than assumed known
cases.reference: a 5000 mas/yr source at 4 pc moves a measurable distance in 1000 yr, and the rectilinear validity warning fires past 1e5 yr while staying silent within it

cases.computed_description: worst residual 2.2737e-13 yr in at most 5 iterations; 10 pc gives 3.2616e+01 yr against 3.2616e+01
cases.expected_description: converged everywhere, and the analytic value at 10 pc
cases.name: c0.light_time_iteration_converges
cases.notes: three states are kept distinct: catalogue-coordinate, geometric at the observer time, and apparent retarded. NO relativistic aberration -- that is C1, and it is absent rather than approximated
cases.reference: the light-time fixed point converges for every nearby source, and for a stationary star at 10 pc gives 32.6 yr

cases.computed_description: sigma_position = 5.0000e-02 pc, sigma_velocity = 4.0910e-07 pc/yr, Jacobian by centred finite differences
cases.expected_description: the dominant parallax term recovered within 5 per cent
cases.name: c0.covariance_transformation
cases.notes: the Jacobian method is LABELLED and travels with the result. HyPAD is not used here: the scalar carries three derivative directions and this Jacobian needs six inputs, so batching costs six evaluations against twelve for centred differences with no accuracy gain
cases.reference: Sigma_y = J Sigma_x J^T reproduces the expected radial uncertainty for a source on the +x axis, sigma_x = d * sigma_parallax/parallax

cases.expected_description: strictly growing
cases.name: c0.uncertainty_grows_with_epoch
cases.notes: written out from the model rather than differenced, because for x = x0 + v dt the expression is exact
cases.reference: the propagated position uncertainty grows with the propagation interval, as Sigma_xx + dt(Sigma_xv + Sigma_vx) + dt^2 Sigma_vv

cases.computed_description: missing rv and missing covariance both flagged; covariance reported as UNKNOWN rather than zero
cases.expected_description: validity bits clear, flags set, covariance refused
cases.name: c0.missing_fields_are_flagged_not_nan
cases.notes: NaN alone never expresses missing data here. An absent uncertainty reported as zero would be the most dangerous possible default
cases.reference: a missing radial velocity and a missing covariance are expressed by CLEAR VALIDITY BITS and quality flags, and the covariance path refuses to report an uncertainty it does not have

cases.expected_description: all fields preserved, schema version 1
cases.name: c0.snapshot_schema_round_trip
cases.notes: floats are written with %.17g, so the round trip is exact rather than close
cases.reference: the snapshot writes and reads back with every identifier, validity bitmask, quality bitmask, estimator and float preserved

cases.expected_description: byte-identical and checksum verified
cases.name: c0.snapshot_is_deterministic
cases.notes: records are written in ascending source_id and the checksum covers the canonical serialization excluding its own line. The checksum is an integrity check against corruption and reordering, NOT a cryptographic guarantee, and is labelled so in the manifest
cases.reference: serialising twice gives byte-identical output and the checksum in the file matches a recomputation

cases.expected_description: validity bits 1..128 and quality bits 1..64 in declared order
cases.name: c0.flag_bit_values_are_pinned
cases.notes: adding a flag means appending a bit; reordering or reusing one silently reinterprets every snapshot ever written
cases.reference: the ValidField and QualityFlag bit values are fixed, because the snapshot stores them as integers that external tools must decode

cases.expected_description: the three published vectors reproduce exactly
cases.name: c0.checksum_matches_published_fnv1a_vectors
cases.notes: the offset basis is 0xcbf29ce484222325 and the prime is 0x100000001b3; tools/import_gaia.py --verify-format checks the same agreement from outside the C++ build
cases.reference: fnv1a() reproduces the published FNV-1a 64-bit test vectors, so an independent implementation can read what this one writes

cases.computed_description: release pinned to Gaia DR3; ADQL 564 characters stored beside the result
cases.expected_description: provenance and the exact ADQL both survive
cases.name: c0.provenance_is_retained_through_the_snapshot
cases.reference: every record still carries its source catalogue, release, table, timestamp, licence and original identifier after a write and read

cases.expected_description: Gaia DR3, gaiadr3.gaia_source, J2016.0
cases.name: c0.catalogue_release_is_pinned
cases.notes: migration to Gaia DR4 must be a deliberate versioned update with regression tests, exactly as the OTIlib pin is enforced elsewhere
cases.reference: the snapshot records the pinned catalogue, table and reference epoch, so a silent migration to a later release fails here

cases.computed_description: 2 within 5 pc, 10 within 50 pc, 1 exoplanet hosts
cases.expected_description: all four queries return results, 5 pc a subset of 50 pc
cases.name: c0.offline_queries_after_import
cases.notes: network access is not part of the simulation runtime: this header reads files and nothing else, and the online client lives in tools/
cases.reference: the 5 pc and 50 pc volume queries, the nearest-N query and the exoplanet-host query all run against the LOADED snapshot with no network access

cases.expected_description: alias resolves to the host, and the host carries its planet
cases.name: c0.identifier_enrichment_and_exoplanet_association
cases.notes: SIMBAD supplies names and cross-identifications only; it is never the primary star catalogue
cases.reference: a source is findable by an alias as well as its primary name, and a planet record is associated with its host

cases.expected_description: one duplicate collapsed, count preserved
cases.name: c0.duplicate_sources_collapse_and_are_counted
cases.reference: the same source_id offered twice yields one record, and the collapse is counted rather than silent

cases.computed_description: delivered 13 in = 11 + 2 + 0; with an injected duplicate 14 in = 11 accepted + 2 rejected + 1 collapsed
cases.expected_description: both ledgers balance and every rejection is explained
cases.name: c0.no_record_is_silently_dropped
cases.notes: this is the case that makes the acceptance criterion '0 silently dropped records' checkable rather than aspirational
cases.reference: rows in equals accepted plus rejected plus duplicates collapsed, and every rejection carries a reason

cases.expected_description: five frames fully described
cases.name: c0.every_frame_declares_its_six_facts
cases.notes: an anonymous Vec3 never crosses a frame boundary: each frame is a distinct type and every transformation is a named function between two named types, so the substitution is a compile error
cases.reference: all five coordinate frames declare frame, origin, orientation, epoch, units and velocity convention

cases.computed_description: checked with std::is_convertible on Parsec, KmPerSecond, Metre, MasPerYear and Degree
cases.expected_description: all five conversions rejected at compile time
cases.name: c0.no_unit_ambiguous_public_field
cases.notes: milliarcseconds against arcseconds, parsecs against light-years, km/s against pc/yr: each has produced published errors, so each has its own type and the compiler refuses the mixture
cases.reference: the unit types are not implicitly constructible from double and do not implicitly interconvert

cases.name: c0.literature_reference_sanity
cases.notes: a LOOSE order-of-magnitude sanity check on the arithmetic, and nothing more. These parallaxes are recorded from memory and must be replaced by a real import before any result depending on them is quoted; no precision assertion rests on them
cases.parameters: 3 stars, values RECALLED not retrieved, tolerance 1 per cent
cases.reference: inverse parallax reproduces the recalled approximate distances of three well-known nearby stars

title: C0-CATALOGUE-UNIVERSE: astronomical data schema, catalogue ingestion, typed coordinate frames, epoch propagation, light time, uncertainty and a deterministic offline snapshot
